title: How Steve Jobs hires A players: results, gut feel, and arguing under pressure
summary: In a 1990s interview for a Stanford-student book, Jobs explains why great people come first, why he spends a fifth of his time recruiting, and how he spots A players by their results and how they hold up under pressure. He also reflects on his liberal arts strength, his idealism, and why the work itself motivates teams.

principles.text: Quality starts with people; there are no shortcuts around it.
principles.quote: There are no shortcuts around quality, and quality starts with people.

principles.text: Spend serious time recruiting, even as a leader: about a day a week.
principles.quote: I spend 20 percent of my time recruiting, even now. I spend a day a week helping people recruit.

principles.text: Find A players by tracing great results back to who was responsible, not by résumés that tell a good story.
principles.quote: I look at great results and I find out who was responsible for them.

principles.text: For young candidates without track records, evaluate potential: intelligence, fast learning, drive and passion.
principles.quote: the primary attributes of potential are intelligence and the ability to learn quickly.

principles.text: Hiring is a gut call that sharpens with experience, so study your hits and misses.
principles.quote: As you hire people over time, your gut instinct gets better and more precise.

principles.text: Test candidates under pressure; you want people who push back with conviction, not those who fold.
principles.quote: What I look for is for someone to come right back and say, “You’re dead wrong and here’s why.”
